title: Undercurrents Surging
next_chapter_hook: At the moment when Chen Ji's fingers were about to touch that activation mark, he saw—a chessboard covering the entire continent, with both him and Chen Nian merely pieces about to be captured on that board.

text.content: That uncanny fluctuation not belonging to the mortal world was like materialized coldness, surging逆流 along the meridians and rushing directly into the Mental Sea. Chen Ji pressed one hand against his chest, and where his fingertips touched, that Imperial Mark was trembling at a terrifying frequency, each tremor seeming to respond to some distant and powerful existence.

dialogue.content: "It has awakened." The Residual Soul Guardian's voice rang in the Mental Sea, the usually calm tone rare带上凝重, "This mark is not an ordinary tracking technique, but... a key. Boy, you are currently being watched by a door that shouldn't exist."

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcefully suppressing the turmoil不安 in his Mental Sea. The Tianji Record Fragment in the depths of consciousness glowed faintly with warmth, the instinct to foresee the future stirring—but he forcefully severed that impulse. The price of three shichen, without understanding the opponent's true strength, must not be paid lightly.

dialogue.content: "Watched?" Chen Ji冷笑 in his heart, his expression unchanged, "For the guardian of the Tianji Record to use words like 'shouldn't exist,' it seems the water behind the Empire runs deeper than I imagined." He stood up, walked to the window, gazing at the moon obscured by dark clouds in the direction of the Imperial Capital, "Since it wants to watch, let it watch its fill."

text.content: Just then, a jet-black carrier pigeon flew through the window and landed on Chen Ji's desk. Tied to its claw was a bamboo tube carved with skull patterns—Ye Qing's unique intelligence delivery method. Chen Ji removed the silk cloth from the bamboo tube, bearing only a few sparse words: "Xuanwu changes, pieces waver."

dialogue.content: Almost at the same moment, a cold transmission pierced through重重禁制 and entered directly into Chen Ji's Mental Sea: "Young Master Chen, the Imperial emissary secretly met Xuanwu Sect's Han Lie last night, promising him the Sect Master position in exchange for... the promise to hand you over." Ye Qing's voice carried a rare killing intent, "Han Lie that fool seems tempted."

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes narrowed slightly. Han Lie, that simple-minded yet heaven-defying combat powerhouse, was indeed unreliable. But he remembered the piece he had planted beside Han Lie—Xuanwu Sect Outer Elder Zhou Chen, an old fox who appeared greedy and cowardly but was actually ambitious to the core. Zhou Chen would never sit by and watch Han Lie monopolize power.

dialogue.content: "Saint Ye Qing," Chen Ji's voice was unhurried, carrying a composure that made backs chill, "Help me investigate someone—whom Zhou Chen has recently met, what he has received, and..." he paused, a meaningful arc curving his lips, "What he truly desires most."

"You're planning to..." Ye Qing was so clever, instantly understanding Chen Ji's intent, "Let Zhou Chen deal with Han Lie?" She fell silent for a moment, then added复杂地, "I've already found some things. Behind the Empire, there seems to be an existence older than the Holy Sect. Be careful."

text.content: Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze passing over the重屋脊 of the Imperial Capital, as if penetrating the遮天蔽日 clouds. He thought of his sister Chen Nian, missing for years—the girl taken by the Holy Sect to become the "Heavenly Fate Lock Key." The Tianji Record always showed blurry visions when foreshadowing anything related to her.

"Chen Nian..." Chen Ji whispered softly, a trace of tenderness flickering in his eyes, immediately replaced by deeper coldness. No matter what stood behind the Empire, whether Han Lie betrayed him or not, he would never let anyone harm his sister. Even if the cost was the entire world.

choice.prompt: Imperial forces have begun their layout, and cracks have appeared within Xuanwu Sect. Facing this chaotic game, Chen Ji must make a choice—

choices.description: Withdraw outer pieces, strengthen core stronghold defense, remain static and await opportunity. Conservative but may miss the initiative.
choices.visible_reward: Preserve core strength, avoid direct confrontation
choices.risk_hint: May allow hostile forces to grow stronger

text.content: "Good." Ye Qing's voice came from the Mental Sea, "My pieces here will暂时按兵不动, waiting for your signal." She paused, a trace of concern in her tone, "Be careful too, don't carry everything alone."

After cutting the transmission, Chen Ji stood alone by the window. His fingers lightly tapped the window lattice, the rhythm unhurried—this was his habit when thinking. Defensive holding was not cowardice, but waiting for the optimal moment to strike. He recorded Han Lie's betrayal, but this debt... will be settled another day.

choices.description: Exploit Zhou Chen's ambition, provoke internal strife in Xuanwu Sect. Seize victory in chaos, but higher risk and may expose more trump cards.
choices.visible_cost: Expose Part of the Intelligence Network
choices.visible_reward: Xuanwu Sect civil strife weakens enemy's overall strength

text.content: Chen Ji drew a jade token engraved with the Xuanwu Sect emblem from his sleeve—a 'token of allegiance' that Zhou Chen had personally handed him. A faint smile curved his lips as he injected a thread of divine sense into it: 'Elder Zhou, long time no see. Han Lie is preparing to betray you—I believe you'd very much like to know what price he quoted.'

A moment later, the jade token warmed slightly, and Zhou Chen's response came: 'What does Young Master Chen want?' Chen Ji did not answer directly, but asked in return: 'What does Elder Zhou want?' Silence stretched on the other end, then a low voice came through: 'Han Lie's death.'

choices.description: Using the intelligence about the Empire's movements to form new alliances with other forces. A grander scheme but requires more leverage.
choices.risk_hint: Whether new allies can be trusted remains unknown

text.content: Chen Ji turned back to his writing desk, spreading a blank silk scroll. The strokes of his brush were sharp, each carrying resolve—he sought to unite not just the sects, but also the small and medium forces oppressed by the Empire, and even... the powers within the Demonic Path who also harbored grievances against the Holy Sect.

"Ye Qing," he transmitted again, "you mentioned there are fractures within the Holy Sect—among those pawns who were used, is there anyone willing to change masters?" Ye Qing fell silent for a long while, her voice carrying a hint of surprise: "You're crazier than I imagined. Still... I like it."

Just then, the Empire's Mark on his chest vibrated violently again, and a stream of information forcibly flooded Chen Ji's Mental Sea—a blurry vision: deep within the Imperial Capital's palace, countless rune formations layered upon each other, and at the very core, a hazy figure slowly lifted its head, as if gazing across infinite distance directly at him.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji stumbled backward sharply, cold sweat beading on his forehead. That figure... gave him a sensation of extreme familiarity yet extreme strangeness, as if it was someone he should recognize, yet could never recall. "Heavenly Dao's Eye..." he murmured, an unprecedented chill surging in his heart.

"Don't look at it." The Soul Fragment Guardian's voice suddenly turned urgent, "It cannot strike you directly yet, but it's probing—probing whether the master of the Tianji Record has appeared. Lad, did you just use your Foresight Ability?" Chen Ji shook his head: "No." "Then it's worse," Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a rare hint of wariness, "It's testing your instinct."

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, sinking his consciousness deep into the Mental Sea. The Tianji Record Fragment floated quietly in the void, its yellowed surface bearing faint ancient patterns. He attempted to touch those patterns with his divine sense—instantly, countless pieces of information surged like a tide, only to shatter into blurry fragments upon touching his consciousness.

choice.prompt: The Tianji Record seemed to be conveying some kind of message, but the fragmented content was difficult to decipher. Chen Ji must make a choice—

choices.description: Burning Heavenly Fate Value to forcibly piece together complete information. Tremendous cost but may gain critical intelligence.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain complete intelligence about the forces behind the Empire
choices.risk_hint: May damage the Tianji Record Fragment

text.content: Chen Ji gritted his teeth, urging the spiritual energy in his body. Heavenly Fate Value surged from within like a boiling spring, pouring into the Tianji Record Fragment. The fragment trembled violently, the scattered patterns beginning to reorganize—but for every pattern combined, his soul felt as if being torn apart by excruciating pain.

Gradually, a complete pattern emerged before his eyes—a chessboard covering the entire continent, with the three characters "Tianji Record" carved prominently at its center. He finally understood: the Tianji Record was no divine weapon, but a key—a key capable of overturning the entire game.

choices.description: Temporarily abandon interpretation, focusing attention on the game at hand. Sometimes, not knowing the whole truth is itself a protection.
choices.visible_reward: Preserve strength, wait for a safer opportunity

text.content: Chen Ji withdrew his divine sense and slowly opened his eyes. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his Mental Sea, carrying a hint of praise: "You made the right choice. Hasty success is the most common mistake clever people make." He paused, adding, "However, there are some things you will eventually need to know."

Chen Ji did not press further. He knew Mo Xiansheng's rule—only after completing one scroll's objective would a page of knowledge be unsealed. Pressing now would yield nothing but ambiguous answers. He redirected his focus to the current situation: Han Lie's betrayal, Zhang Shen's ambition, the ancient existence behind the empire... The chess game was becoming increasingly intriguing.

Night deepened, and the noise of the imperial capital gradually quieted. Chen Ji sat alone beneath the lamplight, a complex network diagram of power spread before him—each node a carefully placed piece, each connection a testament to countless days and nights of strategic planning. Yet now, those lines were being eroded and distorted by an invisible force.

dialogue.content: "Han Lie..." Chen Ji murmured the name softly, his finger pausing at a certain node. That was a piece he had placed high hopes on—the number one genius of Xuanwu Sect, with reversed Combat Power and ambitious dreams, seemingly the easiest to manipulate. But facts proved that once a fool harbored ambition, he became more dangerous than a clever person.

text.content: Chen Ji's gaze swept across the power map, ultimately fixing on a deliberately blank spot—where Chen Nian's name should have been, but was instead shrouded in a faint mist. The Tianji Record persistently failed to reveal what lay beyond. His fingers traced that empty space, pressing down with subtle force.

dialogue.content: "Chen Nian, just wait a moment more." His voice was delicate, as if fearing to disturb something. "Brother will definitely find you." No sooner had the words fallen than a mournful crow's cry sounded from beyond the window. Chen Ji looked up to see a pitch-black crow perched on the eave, fixing him with crimson eyes.

text.content: Under the crow's talons was a yellowed slip of paper. Frowning, Chen Ji plucked the paper away—the text contained a single serpentine line: "Your sister is well, do not worry." Below, a seal he had never encountered yet somehow recognized was stamped. The mark's design mirrored the imperial sigil branded upon his chest.

choice.prompt: Chen Nian's message arrives abruptly, penned in unfamiliar script yet bearing the imperial seal. What could this signify?

choices.description: Immediately mobilize intelligence networks to trace this crow and the paper's origin. Take the initiative, but risk revealing deeper intentions.
choices.risk_hint: If they dare send a message, traps likely await

text.content: Chen Ji tucked the note into his sleeve, then transmitted a divine sense command: "Investigate this crow's origins. I must know who is raising such malevolent creatures in the imperial capital." Moments later, a voice emerged from the shadows: "Master, these crows are called 'Blood Eye Crows', and only core figures of the Holy Sect can command them."

Holy Sect. Chen Ji's gaze turned abruptly cold and sharp. The connection between the empire and the Holy Sect appeared far deeper than he had initially suspected. He pressed further: "Within the Holy Sect, who would most likely have access to the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'?" After a momentary pause, the shadowed figure responded: "Only the Sect Master himself, and... the Supreme Elder Ling Yuan."

choices.description: Stay inactive, waiting for the opponent's next move. Sometimes, the prey needs more patience than the hunter.
choices.visible_cost: Unable to confirm Chen Nian's status for now
choices.visible_reward: Preserve hidden cards, do not expose weaknesses
choices.risk_hint: The other party might be using this to test your bottom line

text.content: Chen Ji carefully folded the note and concealed it in the most hidden pocket against his chest. He asked no questions, showed no anger, and ensured no one knew of the paper's existence. Yet deep within his mind, he was already strategizing—if the other party sought to lure out the snake, he would do the opposite.

"Do not worry?" Chen Ji's lips curved into a cold smile. He raised the note to his nose and inhaled gently—amid the faint decay, there was a whisper of lotus fragrance. It was the scent Chen Nian had cherished since childhood. Closing his eyes, he imprinted that subtle aroma deeply into his memory.

choices.text: Turn the enemy's scheme to one's own advantage
choices.description: Since the other side proactively sent a letter, use this to transmit false intelligence. Neither retreat nor advance, instead turn their force against them.
choices.visible_cost: Need to precisely grasp the scale of information.
choices.visible_reward: May let the other side obtain false intelligence.
choices.risk_hint: Once exposed, it will completely reveal the intentions.

text.content: Chen Ji spread out a blank slip of paper again, picked up his pen and wrote several lines—on the surface expressing dissatisfaction with the imperial envoy's arrogant attitude, but in reality hinting that the protection of Chen Ji within the Tianqing Sect was not a solid block. He folded the paper into a specific shape and tied it to the leg of the same blood-eyed crow.

"Go." He gently patted the crow's wings and watched it vanish into the night. This was a dangerous move—if the other side was clever enough, they would read the exact opposite meaning between the lines. But Chen Ji was betting on this: arrogant people always only believe what they want to believe.

When the eastern sky turned white, Chen Ji had been sitting枯坐了一整夜枯坐在棋盘前。Scattered across the desk were dozens of papers filled with speculations and strategic layouts, each one his analysis and prediction of this chaotic situation. Morning light filtered through the window lattice, illuminating the hidden exhaustion in his eyes, as well as the meaningful smile at the corner of his lips.

The ancient existence behind the empire, the gaze of the Eye of Heaven, Han Lie's betrayal, Chen Nian's safety... All the clues intertwined in Chen Ji's mind, forming an increasingly clear picture. He finally saw the main thread hidden behind everything—the Eternal Chess Game. And he, Chen Ji, would never be anyone's chess piece.

dialogue.content: "Since you want to play chess," Chen Ji rose to his feet, setting all the papers ablaze, the flames reflecting his expression so calm it was almost cold, "then I'll play this game to the end." He pushed open the window, letting the cold morning wind pour in, scattering the last wisp of smoke. The capital's commotion was awakening, a new day, a new chess game.

text.content: Just then, the imperial mark on his chest pulsed again—an异样波动—more intense and aggressive than last night. Chen Ji lowered his head to look, only to see faint text appearing on the mark's surface, like an invitation, yet also a warning. And the content of that text made his pupils suddenly contract.

"The one entering the game: Chen Ji." Those words seemed to carry a蛊惑人心的力量, causing Chen Ji to involuntarily want to reach out and touch. He knew this was a trap, the Tianji Record Fragment was frantically vibrating in the depths of his consciousness, warning him not to approach. But so what? Since fate insists on dragging him into this game, he would overturn the entire chessboard, letting the chess players witness what truly means to be—flawless in calculation.
